newsitem.title: UK: UK pop star backs down on drugs after outcry.
newsitem.headline: UK pop star backs down on drugs after outcry.

text.p: The lead singer of one of Britain's most popular rock groups was forced to apologise on Thursday for remarks in favour of Ecstasy which drew a furious reaction from politicians and the public.
Brian Harvey, 22, of chart-topping London band East 17 at first went on radio to sing the praises of Ecstasy, saying the illegal, mind-altering drug was safe and brought out people's good qualities.
"If it brings out the better in someone -- and really in the long run, it's a safe pill and it ain't doing you no harm -- I don't see the problem," he told Independent Radio News.
The remarks caused a storm of protest and even Prime Minister John Major denounced the singer in parliament.
"Drug taking, any drug taking, leads to hard drugs and we have seen often enough the tragedy that occurs," Major said.
A series of highly publicised deaths linked to Ecstasy has made the drug -- a favourite with millions of young people -- a hot political topic.
Angry listeners bombarded radio shows demanding that East 17's records be banned, and 14 stations obliged.
Eventually, Harvey was forced to issue a retraction.

"Now that I know more about the deadly dangers of Ecstasy, I realise I was completely out of order and am horrified at the thought that anything I said could influence anyone," he said in a statement.

"Without knowing any facts, I now realise that I was being very irresponsible and I would like to apologise as I've obviously caused offence," "All I'd like to say now is...never take Ecstasy -- it can kill you."
